paper.title: On Multi-Armed Bandit Designs for Dose-Finding Clinical Trials

settings.name_in_paper: MTD identification (number of sub-optimal dose selections)
unmapped: Optimal arm is the arm whose mean is closest to a known target threshold theta (MTD), not the arm with largest mean
Performance measured by expected number of selections of each sub-optimal dose rather than regret
Learner knows the target toxicity threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: Denoting by $p_k$ the (unknown) toxicity probability of dose $k$, the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) is defined as the dose with a toxicity probability closest to a target: $k^* \in \argmin_{k} |\theta - p_k|$ ... this second objective can be formalized as that of minimizing $N_k(n)$ for $k\neq k^*$.

unmapped: Goal is to identify, with a fixed budget n, the arm whose mean is closest to a known threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: Minimizing the error probability for MTD can be viewed as a variant of the fixed-budget Best Arm Identification (BAI) problem ... the focus is on identifying the arm whose mean is closest to the threshold $\theta$.

symbols.d_k_star: element of {p_{k*}, 2 theta - p_{k*}} closest to p_k
symbols.C_eps: constant depending on eps, threshold theta and the toxicity probabilities

conditions: k is such that |p_k - theta| != |theta - p_{k*}|
Bound on E[N_k(n)], the expected number of selections of sub-optimal dose k
tuning: independent uniform priors on each p_k

source.label: thm:TS
source.quote: Independent Thompson Sampling satisfies the following. For all $\varepsilon >0$, there exists a constant $C_{\varepsilon,\theta,\bm p}$ ... such that for all $k : |p_k - \theta| \neq |\theta - p_{k^*}|$, \bE[N_{k}(n)] \leq \frac{1 + \varepsilon}{\mathrm{kl}(p_k,d_k^*)} \log(n) + C_{\varepsilon,\theta,\bm p}

results.notes: Per-arm pull-count bound (quantity other). The paper also derives P(k_hat != k*) <= D ln(n)/n informally from this result (eq. UpperBoundError), not recorded separately.

symbols.d_k_star: element of {p_{k*}, 2 theta - p_{k*}} closest to p_k

conditions: uniformly efficient design: E[N_k(n)] = o(n^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1) and all sub-optimal k on every instance

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: We define a uniformly efficient design as a design satisfying for all possible toxicity probabilities $\bm p$, for all $\alpha \in ]0,1[$, ... $\bE[N_k(n)] = o(n^\alpha)$ ... If $p_{k^*} \neq \theta$, any uniformly efficient design satisfies ... \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\bE[N_k(n)]}{\log(n)} \geq \frac{1}{\mathrm{kl}(p_k,d_k^*)}.

results.notes: Lai-Robbins type lower bound on pull counts for the MTD problem.

symbols.H_2: max_{k != k*} k * Delta_[k]^{-2}, with Delta_k = |p_k - theta| - |p_{k*} - theta| sorted increasingly

source.label: thm:SH
source.quote: The error probability of the \texttt{SH} algorithm is upper bounded as \bP\left(\hat{k}_n \neq k^*\right) \leq 9 \log_2 K \cdot \exp \left( - \frac{n}{8 H_2 (\bm p)\log_2 K} \right), where $H_2(\bm p):= \max_{k \ne k^*} {k}{\Delta_{[k]}^{-2}}$ ...

results.notes: Paper's n is the budget T. Error probability is a probability bound; 'probability' field set to high_probability as closest option.
